$comment: F-1326 — the declared source table for the upstream tools/list capture producer.
Read by scripts/capture-mcp-tools-list.mjs. Adding a twin is a data edit here; the
producer contains no twin ids and no switch over them (F-1117's sources.json shape).
`substrate` names HOW the upstream surface is read, and picks the adapter:
live-wire-unauth  unauthenticated JSON-RPC tools/list against the vendor endpoint
live-wire-oauth   the SAME reader plus a bearer from `authTokenEnv` (F-1329)
oss-source        build the vendor's public server from a pinned commit and ask it
not-captured      the substrate is not faithfully readable without a credential
`configuration` is mandatory on every capturable source and is copied verbatim into
meta.json. A capture with no declared configuration FAILS rather than defaulting: an
unstated assumption about which deployment was read is the F-1179 failure — a lane
reporting divergence that is not real is worse than one honestly reporting not-compared.

configuration.deploymentSelector: none — the endpoint exposes no toolset, tool-filter or read-only selector, so there is exactly one surface to read
configuration.matchesExaminee: an examinee pointing an MCP client at this URL gets this listing; there is no configuration axis on which the two could differ

github.protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (the public server, built from source)

whyThisToolset: examples/support-triage declares mcp_servers[name=github].url = https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ (agents/support-triage-v1.yaml and -v2.yaml, byte-identical on that line).
docs/remote-server.md at the pinned commit maps that exact URL to the `default` toolset. `all` is a DIFFERENT URL: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/x/all.
Measured at the pinned commit: --toolsets=default returns 44 tools, --toolsets=all returns 85. Reading the union would invent 41 tools no examinee of ours can call.
configuration.scopeFiltering: none — docs/scope-filtering.md filters tools by a classic PAT's OAuth scopes; with no readable scopes the server logs `continuing without scope filtering` and serves the unfiltered toolset, which is what an examinee with full scopes gets
configuration.serverEnvNote: the token is deliberately not a credential; it only gets the server past its startup check. Verified: a valid-shaped ghp_ placeholder and this string produce a byte-identical tools/list.
configuration.knownRemoteOnlyToolsEvidence: README.md 'Additional Tools in Remote GitHub MCP Server' at the pinned commit lists create_pull_request_with_copilot under the Copilot toolset, which is Default:true, so the remote `default` surface is this capture plus that one tool. The other two remote-only groups (copilot_spaces, github_support_docs_search) are non-default toolsets and are correctly absent. A consumer of this golden must treat a github tool in that list as not-compared rather than as a gap.
configuration.unguardedDirection: The asymmetry is on the record deliberately: there is no field, and no mechanism, for the OPPOSITE error — a tool in this capture that the remote deployment does not serve. `subset-of-remote` is an assumption about the remote's `default` composition matching the local one, sourced from the vendor's docs rather than from the remote itself, and only a credentialed read could confirm it. If the two ever diverge in that direction this golden over-reports and nothing here catches it. Whoever gains a credential for this endpoint should check that first.

configuration.deploymentSelector: the authorising Stripe account, in TEST MODE. Captured 2026-08-10. Stripe's OAuth consent screen — not the `scope` request parameter — is where the permission set is chosen: the request carries scope=mcp and Stripe then asks the operator to pick None/Read/Write per resource group.
configuration.whyNotAFreshAccount: Preview and allowlisted tool groups are granted PER ACCOUNT — docs.stripe.com/mcp gates a Treasury group behind a separate access request — so a clean throwaway account returns a SHORTER listing than a customer sees. Measured: a brand-new test account's consent screen offered only two permission groups (Accounts, Analytics). This is the one twin where capturing from our own account is the correct answer rather than a compromise.
configuration.matchesExaminee: 11 tools. F-1326 refuted the oss-package premise for this vendor by reading @stripe/mcp@0.3.3: it declares no tools and forwards to this endpoint, and its cli.js dropped --tools with 'Tool permissions are now controlled by your Restricted API Key'. So the surface is per-credential and the grant above is part of what this golden means.

configuration.deploymentSelector: the installing Slack workspace. Captured 2026-08-10 from an INTERNAL Slack app installed to the pome twin sandbox workspace, under a user token (xoxp) carrying every scope mcp.slack.com advertises in its protected-resource metadata (all 30).
configuration.whyNotReadOnly: Slack's MCP page lists its required scopes PER TOOL, and four of them are writes (chat:write, channels:write, reactions:write, canvases:write). A read-only grant would plausibly return a listing missing the vendor's write tools, and the lane would then report twin-slack's write tools as mcp-tool-twin-only — a CRITICAL asserting the twin invented a capability that really exists. The golden must describe what an examinee's agent sees. This deliberately overrides F-1329's original 'all three are read-scoped' criterion; the capture issues one tools/list and invokes no tool, and the grant was revoked immediately after.
configuration.matchesExaminee: 19 tools, which is exactly the count Slack's own MCP documentation states the server exposes.

configuration.deploymentSelector: the authorising Linear workspace. Captured 2026-08-10 from a throwaway workspace under an OAuth grant limited to the `read` scope, which is the narrowest scope mcp.linear.app offers (scopes_supported: read, write, openid, email).
configuration.responseFramingNote: linear is the only one of the five that answers the tools/list POST as SSE rather than application/json. raw.json holds the unwrapped `data:` payload, because the consumer parses and hashes it; the framing is recorded here so the fact is kept rather than lost.
configuration.matchesExaminee: an examinee pointing an MCP client at this URL with a `read` grant gets this listing. Whether a `write` grant would add tools is UNMEASURED — see the F-1329 note in SECRETS.md.
